claim: Oakberry's first kiosk in Sao Paulo (2016) measured only 6 m2; the company reached nearly 100 stores in Brazil between 2016 and 2018 before expanding internationally, opened its first international unit in Orlando (Florida Mall) in July 2018 via a 50/50 structure with a local operator, concluded after two additional Florida kiosks in 2018 that the 50/50 model was not sustainable for rapid scaling (shifting to a local franchisor office and territorial master franchisees), and entered China (Shanghai) in 2021.
evidence_quote: “A franqueadora tinha 50% do negócio e o operador local, 50%.”
corrected_value: Source supports 6 m² São Paulo kiosk (2016), Florida Mall (2018), 50/50 ownership, two later Florida kiosks and master franchisees; not July, nearly 100 by 2018, or Shanghai 2021.

claim: Founder Georgios Frangulis stated that scalability was a priority from day one; in the U.S. market Oakberry's preferred store footprint is approximately 46.5 m2 (~500 sq. ft.), with estimated unit investment of US$100,000 to US$320,000, a staffing model of 1 employee during normal shifts and up to 3 at peak periods, and a customizable bowl built from a standardized organic acai base, cup size, and predefined toppings.

Oakberry's U.S. franchise framework specifies store formats ranging from compact kiosks to shops (500 to 1,500 sq. ft.) and estimated initial investment of US$150,000 to US$320,000, using a bounded cold-assembly workflow (standardized acai base dispensed in 3 cup sizes with layered cold toppings).
corrected_value: Linked PDF is a 2022 Sustainability Bond Framework, not a U.S. franchise framework; it does not state the claimed format, investment or workflow.

claim: By year-end 2025, OAK Holding S.A. reported 982 stores globally (373 in Brazil and 609 abroad); consolidated financials (R$ million) show net revenue rising from R$173.2m (2023) to R$264.8m (2024) and R$441.0m (2025), operating result moving from +R$19.4m (2023) and +R$19.3m (2024) to -R$11.1m (2025), net income/(loss) moving from +R$2.1m (2023) to -R$3.1m (2024) and -R$88.4m (2025), operating cash flow negative across all three years (-R$8.8m in 2023, -R$43.2m in 2024, -R$32.1m in 2025), and PPE + intangible investment rising from R$33.5m (2023) and R$44.1m (2024) to R$162.0m (2025).
evidence_quote: “Em 31 de dezembro de 2025, o Grupo possuía 982 unidades.”
corrected_value: 2025/2024 only: revenue R$441.0m/R$264.8m; operating result R$-11.1m/R$19.3m; net loss R$-88.4m/R$-3.1m; operating cash flow R$-32.1m/R$-43.2m; PPE+intangibles investment R$162.0m/R$44.1m. 2023 figures are not in this filing.

claim: OAK Holding S.A.'s 2024 audited financial statements report 2023 and 2024 net revenue of R$173.2m and R$264.8m, operating result of R$19.4m and R$19.3m, net income/(loss) of R$2.1m and -R$3.1m, operating cash flow of -R$8.8m and -R$43.2m, and 2024 debenture issuance of R$100m alongside prior R$50m Green CRA debt (2022).

Oakberry raised R$325 million in a 2023-2024 transaction led by BTG Pactual (following an earlier R$84 million round with Monte Bravo / Kilima in 2021) to accelerate international expansion and verticalized acai production.
corrected_value: R$325m BTG transaction was announced 22 Dec 2023. The source separately says R$84m from Monte Bravo/Kilima in 2021 funded verticalisation; BTG funds targeted international expansion.

claim: Oakberry and Fortitude Capital formed a EUR 14.5 million strategic joint venture (EUR 10.47m from Fortitude Capital and EUR 4.03m from Oakberry) in 2024-2025 to expand Oakberry stores across Southern Europe (Portugal, Spain, and Italy).
evidence_quote: “initial focus in Portugal, Spain and Italy”
corrected_value: Fortitude confirms a Southern Europe JV dated 13 Jan 2025, but discloses neither EUR 14.5m nor the claimed contribution split.

claim: Oakberry entered Indonesia in November 2023 via Bali, operating 4 stores in Bali (Canggu, Ubud, Seminyak) with Jakarta and Surabaya listed as upcoming expansion cities, and still has 0 operating stores in Jakarta on its official Indonesian store locator.
corrected_value: The official locator lists four Bali locations and none in Jakarta; it does not state Indonesia entry timing or Jakarta/Surabaya expansion plans.

claim: Oakberry opened its first Indonesian store in Canggu, Bali on 19 November 2023 (Jl. Munduk Catu No. 3, near Batu Bolong Beach) and its second store in Ubud on 26 November 2023 (Jl. Wanawarna, ~700m from Ubud Monkey Forest), targeting Bali's international tourist, surf, and yoga/wellness circuits first with plans to expand later to Jakarta and Surabaya.
evidence_quote: “11月19日、チャングー ... 26日には2号店がウブド”
corrected_value: The article confirms Canggu on 19 Nov 2023 and Ubud on 26 Nov 2023 at the stated addresses; it does not document tourist-circuit targeting or Jakarta/Surabaya plans.

claim: Oakberry Indonesia's business development representative (Syauqi Al Ibrama) published a call for Jakarta retail spaces seeking premium, brand-aligned sites, reputable landlords/co-tenants, and healthy-lifestyle consumer footfall, and in a separate post highlighted Grand Indonesia, Pondok Indah Mall, and PIK2/Aloha as examples of Jakarta's evolving retail landscape.
evidence_quote: “premium locations ... reputable tenants or landlords ... healthy lifestyle”
corrected_value: The posts show Syauqi Al Ibrama at Oakberry Indonesia seeking premium Jakarta locations, reputable tenants or landlords and healthy-lifestyle consumers; the source says tenants, not co-tenants.
